in_arabic.name: تميز
in_arabic.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root word 'tam' which means 'to send forth' or 'to make known'. The name Tameez can be interpreted as 'one who makes things known' or 'one who spreads knowledge'.

data.cultural_impact: The name Tameez carries a significant cultural impact in the Islamic world, highlighting the importance of kindness, generosity, and teaching in Muslim society. It is an encouragement to spread love, joy, and goodwill, not only among family and close friends but also to all creation, in line with the teachings of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) to "spread peace and security, feed the hungry, and help the afflicted". Moreover, Tameez is a reminder of the Koranic principle of Sadaqah or voluntary giving, which has been an integral aspect of Muslim culture for centuries, providing a safety net for the poor and needy.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Tameez holds great significance as it reflects the unselfish acts of Allah, who out of His infinite Mercy and Love for His Creation, abundantly showers Blessings and Favors upon us. The name also serves as a reminder of the Prophet Muhammad's (pbuh) call for Muslims to be a source of good and a giver of knowledge, spreading the light of Allah's message to the masses. The spiritual messages conveyed by the name Tameez include the importance of gratitude, kindness, generosity, and the blessings of knowledge and wisdom. By deeply embracing the essence of this beautiful name, one cultivates a compassionate, loving, and inspiring spirit that shines bright, reflecting the Divine Light of Allah.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Abdul Barr records that Tameez was a title given to the viceroy of Egypt and Syria during the Umayyad Caliphate. The viceroy was responsible for administering the provinces in the name of the caliph and collecting taxes.
Al-Maqrizi mentions that Tameez was a title given to the ruler of Egypt during the Ayyubid Sultanate. The title signified the power and authority granted to the ruler to govern Egypt.
